label: PF Backlog 501
title: Git-remote CAS id authority (GitHub as the shared allocator) + auto-reconcile duplicate ids at merge/PR
body:
## Problem / why
A per-host id authority is not foolproof: a remote worker that launches with localhost points at its OWN
authority and re-collides. The ONE thing every session/worker already shares is the git remote (GitHub).

## Goal / value
Reserve id blocks through an ATOMIC CAS on the shared git remote, so local and remote sessions use the same
authority with nothing to point at; fall back to the local block; and RECONCILE duplicate ids automatically at
merge/PR.

## In scope
- core/id_allocator: git-remote CAS reservation (dedicated ref refs/heads/pf-id-counter; reserve a block via a
  non-FF git push = compare-and-swap; retry on rejection) as the PRIMARY path; then the API; then the local block.
  PF_ID_ALLOC_REMOTE=off disables.
- scripts/dev/backlog_id_reconcile.py: detect duplicate ids per scope; keep the item that is on
  origin/develop (else earliest created_at) and RENUMBER the incoming one (item id + file + history + all
  references: deps/blocked_by/links.epic/epic children/possible_duplicate_of) + regenerate indexes.
- Wire reconcile into precheck (auto-fix) before the id audit (verify).

## Out of scope
- GitHub Issues as ids; changing the id string format.

links.backend_capability: module:core/id_allocator.py, module:scripts/dev/backlog_id_reconcile.py,
test:test-framework/tests/pipeline/test_id_allocator_git.py

brief.problem: a per-host id authority is not foolproof - a remote worker launching with localhost points at its own authority and re-collides; the only thing every session shares is the git remote
brief.what_adds: reserve id blocks via an atomic CAS on the shared git remote (refs/heads/pf-id-counter), fall back to the local block, and auto-reconcile duplicate ids at merge/PR
brief.why: so local and remote sessions share one authority with nothing to point at, and merges land clean
brief.who_feels: every session/worker that creates backlog items; maintainers (no manual renumbering)

objective: id blocks are reserved via an atomic CAS on the shared git remote and duplicate ids are auto-reconciled at merge
acceptance_criteria: _reserve_git reserves a disjoint block via a non-FF git push (CAS) and retries on rejection
unreachable remote falls back to a local block
backlog_id_reconcile renumbers the incoming duplicate and updates all references + indexes
precheck reconciles then the id audit passes
approach: git fetch the counter ref; reserve [N+1,N+size]; commit + push to the ref (non-FF = CAS) with retry; fall back to API then local block; reconcile renumbers duplicates keeping the base version

divergences: authority becomes the git remote; auto-renumber at merge

verification: test_id_allocator_git.py (temp bare remote: two reserves are disjoint)
risks: git push CAS needs remote write access
auto-renumber at merge mutates the store

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing components/APIs: core/budget_allocator.py, core/github.py, core/id_allocator.py, core/merge_gate.py
